To find the rank of $E,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 20 & 20 & 10 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+10{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(E)=2.$
